Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:99: The third: to be present in the synagogue, whether for prayer or for the study of Torah, if possible - for one who comes to the synagogue is called "one who fears the LORD," as it is said (Isaiah 50:10), "who among you fears the LORD, who hears the voice of His servant, who walks in darkness and has no light?" And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained in tractate Berachot (6b) that this is said of one who is accustomed to come to the synagogue and, one day, does not come; in these words: Ravin bar Rav Adda said in the name of Rav Chisda: whoever is accustomed to come to the synagogue and, one day, does not come - the Holy One, blessed be He, inquires about him, as it is said, "who among you fears the LORD, who hears the voice of His servant, who walks in darkness and has no light? Let him trust in the name of the LORD and rely upon his God" - if he went for a matter of a commandment, he has light; and if he went for a permissible matter [not a commandment], he has no light. Why? Because he should have trusted in the name of the LORD, and he did not trust. And in the Zohar, Parashat Balak (196a), there is a sweet matter in explaining this verse - examine it there, for it pertains to the matter of exposition.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:100: And the reason that one who comes to the synagogue is called "one who fears the LORD" is because the synagogue is a small sanctuary, of which it is said, "and you shall fear My sanctuary." And further, the place of fear because of judgment is the synagogue, for there the shining fire rests upon the heads of Israel, as we shall elaborate in its place.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:101: The fourth: to draw close to everyone who fears the LORD, and to distance oneself from one who does not fear the LORD, even from merely conversing with him in the manner of companionship. And this is learned from what King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 119:63), "I am a companion to all who fear You," and so on. And the reason is that by drawing close to good people, one learns from their deeds; and further, the Shechinah, called "fear," is with them, and the light of the Shechinah will radiate upon him - and the opposite, "but a companion of fools shall be broken" (Proverbs 13:20). And this matter is learned from what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Yoma 9b): whoever conversed with Reish Lakish would be trusted [in business dealings] without a document and without witnesses.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:102: The fifth: it is written (Psalms 34:12), "come, children, listen to me; I will teach you the fear of the LORD. Who is the man who desires life," and so on, "guard your tongue from evil," and so on. It appears that the first levels by which a person ascends in fear are these: first, "guard your tongue from evil," and so on; the second, "turn from evil and do good"; the third, "seek peace," and so on - and we have elaborated in explaining these verses in the Gate of Holiness, chapters 10 and 11. The second, "turn from evil," also pertains to fear, and we explained its matter in chapter 4 of this Gate. "Seek peace" pertains to the matter of "and do good," and we explained it there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:103: The sixth: Isaiah the prophet, peace be upon him, explained, when he said (Isaiah 29:13), "and their fear of Me is a commandment of men, learned by rote." It appears that a person must investigate and know in truth whom he serves and whom he fears - along the lines of what David, peace be upon him, commanded Solomon, peace be upon him (I Chronicles 28:9), "know the God of your father and serve Him." And the reason is that one who serves in the manner of "a commandment of men, learned by rote" will sometimes do so and sometimes not, and his heart is not fixed in faith; and if a Kuti [gentile] or someone like him comes and undermines his faith through arguments and difficulties, he might be defeated. But one who serves through the knowledge of his heart will never be defeated in any way. And the punishment of one who serves as "a commandment of men, learned by rote," the prophet explains afterward, when he says (Isaiah 29:14), "therefore, behold, I will again do a marvelous work among this people, a marvelous and wondrous work; and the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the understanding of their prudent men shall be hidden" - because it is measure for measure: since they did not wish to grow wise in Torah, to know the matter of the fear of the Creator in truth, so wisdom will be lost from the wise.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:104: And along these lines, the place of fear is [the sefirah of] Chochmah [yud], as explained in chapter 2 of this Gate; and therefore one must grow wise in fear, and it should not be "a commandment of men, learned by rote" - and to this it says (Avot 2:5), "an ignoramus cannot fear sin," for if not, Heaven forfend, wisdom, which is the source of fear, will be hidden.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:105: And so too this punishment relates back to what is said at the beginning of the verse: "forasmuch as this people draw near Me with their mouth, and with their lips honor Me, but have removed their heart far from Me, and their fear of Me is," and so on - for since he speaks with his God while the understanding of his heart is not with him, therefore his punishment is that the understanding of his prudent men will be hidden - and thus the entire verse is precise, with nothing superfluous in it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:106: And along these lines, one must also be careful in the recitation of one's prayer and blessings, that they be said with intention, and not be "a commandment of men, learned by rote" - as it says, "with their mouth and their lips they honor Me, but their heart is far from Me," and so on. And it is said in the Sefer Chasidim (section 46): there was an incident with a man who died several years before his time; many years later he appeared in a dream to one of his relatives, who asked him, how do you fare in the world where you are? He said to him: every day they judge me for not having been precise in the blessing over bread, and the blessing over fruit, and the Grace after Meals, with proper intention of heart, and they say to me, you intended it for your own benefit. He asked him: but is not the judgment of the wicked of Israel [in Gehinnom] only twelve months, and more than that has already passed over you, and yet they still judge you? He said to him: they do not judge me with harsh punishments as in the first twelve months - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:107: And among the virtues of fear, in the World to Come: "how great is Your goodness, which You have stored up for those who fear You" (Psalms 31:20); and in this world, being watched over with an open eye, the eye of Arich Anpin, as it is written (ibid. 33:18), "behold, the eye of the LORD is upon those who fear Him, upon those who hope for His kindness"; (ibid. 103:11), "for as high as the heavens are above the earth, so great is His kindness toward those who fear Him," and so on; and likewise (ibid. 103:13), "as a father has compassion on his children, so the LORD has compassion on those who fear Him." And the reason is that the one who fears causes the subduing of the forces of judgment, as explained in the discourse of King David, peace be upon him, and therefore it is fitting that mercy be drawn upon him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:108: And among its virtues is what is mentioned in the psalm (Psalms 112:1-2), "happy is the man who fears the LORD, who delights greatly in His commandments; his descendants shall be mighty in the land," and so on. And among its virtues is that fear brings additional life, as it is written (Proverbs 10:27), "the fear of the LORD prolongs days." And so they said in the Midrash Pesikta (of Rav Kahana, section 27), on the verse (Psalms 16:11), "You shall make known to me the path of life; fullness of joy is in Your presence" - Rabbi Yudan said, David said before the Holy One, blessed be He, "make known to me the path of life." The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: David, do you seek life? Look to fear, as it is said, "the fear of the LORD prolongs days" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 15:109: With this the chapter is concluded, and this Gate is concluded. Blessed be the LORD forever, Amen and Amen:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:1: In explaining the necessity that service be with love, and the nature of the matter of love, as found in the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, and in the books of the earlier pious ones.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:2: That our service should be with love, we are commanded in the Torah, in Deuteronomy, several times - whether in the passage "and now, Israel," as we wrote above, or in the passage of Shema (Deuteronomy 6:5), "and you shall love the LORD your God with all your heart," or in the passage "and it shall come to pass, if you hearken" (ibid. 11:13), "to love the LORD your God and to serve Him." And Rabbeinu Moshe of Coucy wrote in Sefer Mitzvot HaGadol, concerning the commandment to love, in these words: and because this passage is beloved before the Holy One, blessed be He, and it is the key to our fear, for it contains the unity of the Creator and the warning to love His Name with all one's heart, soul, and might - and the whole Torah is included in this, for one who loves the king, all his thoughts are to do what is good and right in his eyes - therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded that five reminders be made of this every day: (1) to recite this passage when he lies down, (2) and when he rises; (3) that this passage be written opposite your heart in the tefillin of the left arm, fixed opposite the heart, as it is said (ibid. 11:18), "and you shall place these words of Mine upon your heart" - and our Rabbis expounded that the placement should be opposite the heart; (4) that this passage be written opposite your soul, that the head-tefillin be placed on the brain, which is aligned opposite the space between the eyes from above, since the essence of the soul's [rational faculty] and the settling of a person's mind is there - and this is (Exodus 13:16), "and they shall be for frontlets between your eyes"; (5) that this passage be written opposite your wealth [me'odecha], on the doorposts of your house and gates, since a person's money is there. And in the order in which they are written in Scripture - heart first, then soul, then wealth - so they were commanded in this order: "and you shall bind them for a sign upon your hand" opposite your heart; "and they shall be for frontlets between your eyes" opposite your soul; "and you shall write them on the doorposts of your house and your gates" opposite your wealth - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:3: And when you examine these five mentioned times, they amount to ten - for in the passage "and it shall come to pass, if you hearken," the matter of love is mentioned, and it is in the tefillin and the mezuzah, and we recite it when we lie down and when we rise.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:4: Further, I found that the commandment to love is mentioned nine times in Deuteronomy: once in Parashat Va'etchanan, in the passage "and you shall love" (Deuteronomy 6:5); four in Parashat Eikev, in the passage "and now, Israel" (ibid. 10:12), where it says "to walk in all His ways and to love Him"; (ibid. 11:1), "and you shall love the LORD your God and keep His charge," and so on; (ibid. 11:13), "to love the LORD your God and to serve Him with all your heart," and so on; (ibid. 11:22), "for if you diligently keep all this commandment which I command you to do it, to love the LORD your God, to walk in all His ways, and to cleave to Him." Further, in Parashat Shoftim it is mentioned once (ibid. 19:9), "to love the LORD your God and to walk in His ways always." And in Parashat Atem Nitzavim it is mentioned three times (ibid. 30:6), "and the LORD your God will circumcise your heart," and so on, "to love the LORD your God," and so on; (ibid. 30:16), "which I command you today, to love the LORD your God, to walk in His ways, and to keep His commandments"; at the end of the passage (ibid. 30:20), "to love the LORD your God, to hearken to His voice, and to cleave to Him" - that makes nine. And the commandment to love the convert, in Parashat Eikev (10:19), makes ten - corresponding to the ten sefirot; and the love of the convert is in the tenth sefirah, called Tzedek [Righteousness], and indeed the convert is called "tzedek" [in halachic terminology]. Behold, the commandment of love is doubled and repeated many times, because it is the root of all divine service, and it is the ultimate purpose of the soul's perfection, that it cleave to its Creator, as it says "to love," and so on, "and to cleave to Him," as will be explained, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:5: And concerning the matter of love, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in the Sifrei, in these words: "and you shall love the LORD your God" - act out of love; for there is a difference between one who acts out of love and one who acts out of fear. One who acts out of love, his reward is doubled and redoubled - for it says, "the LORD your God shall you fear": there is a person who fears his fellow, but when the fellow burdens him too much, he leaves him and goes away; but you, act out of love - for there is no love in the place of fear, nor fear in the place of love, except regarding the attribute of the Omnipresent alone - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:6: Further, in Tanna Devei Eliyahu (Rabbah, chapter 28): what is the difference between love and fear? They gave a parable: to what may this be compared? To a king who had two servants - one loved the king and feared him, and the other feared him but did not love him. The king went to a country overseas. The one who loved the king and feared him arose and planted gardens and orchards and all kinds of choice fruits; the one who feared him but did not love him sat and did nothing. When the king returned from overseas, he saw the gardens and orchards and all kinds of choice fruits arranged before him, according to the mind of the one who loved him; once the lover entered before the king and saw all kinds of choice fruits arranged before him, his mind was set at ease, corresponding to the king's joy. As for the one who feared him but did not love him - once the king entered his house, all kinds of ruins were arranged before him, corresponding to the mind of the fearful one; once the fearful one entered before the king and saw all kinds of ruins arranged before him, his mind trembled, corresponding to the king's wrath - as it is said (Psalms 111:5), "He has given food to those who fear Him" - this refers to this world. Behold, you learn that the reward of the lover is two portions, and the reward of the fearful one is one portion; therefore the wicked merited only this world, but there are those who will enjoy both worlds - this is what the verse says (Song of Songs 8:7), "many waters," and so on, whose ending I copied in chapter 7.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:7: And what emerges for us from the general sense of this discourse is that the essence of love is that a person performs the king's desire in order to gladden him - and even though he knows that from those trees he plants, the king will give him various choice fruits as a reward for what he planted, nevertheless the lover's intent is only that his mind be set at ease corresponding to the king's joy - for the king is glad to see gardens and orchards and trees planted before him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:8: And the analogy is understood: the fearful ones are the idol-worshipping nations, all of whom are fearful, as it says (Jeremiah 10:7), "who would not fear You, King of the nations," and so on, "for among all the wise men of the nations," and so on, "there is none like You" - and it is explained in Parashat Mishpatim (Zohar 95b-96a) that they all admit there is none like Him, but they do not perform commandments; rather, they are [merely] fearful. And the lovers are Israel, who perform commandments; and in the performance of commandments and the occupation with Torah is the planting of trees, planting supernal illuminations above in which the King rejoices - for everything depends on the arousal from below, as I have explained several times. And from the supernal light that they drew down through the performance of commandments, their souls enjoy [it] in the World to Come - along the lines of "one who toils on the eve of Shabbat shall eat on Shabbat."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:9: In [tractate] Nedarim (62a) it is taught: "to love the LORD... and to cleave to Him" (Deuteronomy 30:20) - let a person not say, I will recite [Scripture] so that they call me "wise," I will study [Mishnah] so that they call me "Rabbi," I will study so that I be called an elder and sit in the academy; rather, learn out of love, and honor will come in the end, as it is said (Proverbs 7:3), "bind them upon your fingers, write them on the tablet of your heart," and it says (ibid. 3:17), "her ways are ways of pleasantness," and it says (ibid.), "she is a tree of life" - to this point. Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok says: do things for their own sake, and speak of them for their own sake; do not make them a crown to magnify yourself with, nor a spade to dig with, and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:10: And further, they said in the Midrash (Yalkut Tehillim, section 871), on "who delights greatly in His commandments" - Rabbi Elazar said: in His commandments, but not in the reward of His commandments - and this is what we have learned (Avot 1:3): Antigonus of Socho would say, do not be like servants who serve their master on condition of receiving a reward.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:11: And further, they said in the Sifrei (Eikev 5): "to love" - lest you say, I will learn Torah in order to become wealthy, in order to be called "Rabbi," for the sake of reward in the World to Come - the verse teaches, "to love": whatever you do, do only out of love - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:12: And in the Zohar, Parashat Va'etchanan (267a), they say, in these words, on the verse (Deuteronomy 6:5), "and you shall love the LORD your God" - "and you shall love": a person must bind himself to Him with love, for every supernal service that a person must perform for the Holy One, blessed be He, he must perform with love, for there is no service like the love of the Holy One, blessed be He - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:13: And in the Tikkunim (page 73b) it says that one who serves in order to receive a reward has a punishment; in these words, in brief: but love and fear apply both to good and to evil; and therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, said (Song of Songs 2:7), "I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles and by the hinds of the field, that you not stir up nor awaken love until it please" - meaning, this love and reward, until it wishes [of itself], and not in order to receive reward - for fear and love [performed] in order to receive reward are [merely] a maidservant; "and under three things the earth trembles... under a servant when he becomes king, and a maidservant when she inherits her mistress" (Proverbs 30:21-23) - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:14: And concerning the matter of love, the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot wrote, at the end of the Gate of Trust and in the Gate of Love, and I have gathered his words in brief, insofar as they pertain to our subject (Gate of the Love of God, chapter 1): the matter of love is the longing of the soul and its inclination, in itself, toward the Creator, so that it cleave to His supernal light. This is because the soul is a spiritual essence, inclined toward those similar to it among spiritual beings, and by its nature distances itself from what is opposite it, the coarse bodies; and when the Creator bound it to this coarse body with which He wished to test it, through its governing of it, He aroused it to have pity on it and yearn for it, so as to seek rest from the ailments of its body. But when the soul senses something that adds light to itself and strength to its own being, it inclines with its intent [thought] toward Him, and cleaves to Him in its thought, and desires Him, and yearns for Him - especially when a person knows the purpose intended in his creation and his coming forth into this transient world, and recognizes the greatness of the other, eternal world - he will despise this world and its causes, and flee in his thought, his soul, and his body to God, blessed be He, and delight in remembering Him in solitude, and be astonished at not thinking of His greatness [always]; and if he be in gatherings, he will desire nothing but His will, and yearn for nothing but encountering Him, and his yearning for Him will be with effort, diligence, and alacrity - similar to what is said (Isaiah 26:9), "my soul yearns for You in the night," and so on, and it says (ibid. 26:8), "for Your name and for Your remembrance is the soul's desire," and it says (Psalms 42:3), "my soul thirsts for God, for the living God," and it says (ibid. 63:2), "O God, You are my God; I seek You early; my soul thirsts for You, my flesh longs for You," and so on - and then the soul will be given to drink the elixir of love in God, and will be solitary in the unity of its heart with Him, to love Him and trust in Him and yearn for Him, and will have no occupation but the occupation of His service, and will let nothing pass through its thoughts but Him, and nothing will arise in its thought besides Him, and it will not send forth any limb of its body except in what is drawn toward His name, and will not loosen its tongue except in remembering His praise and thanksgiving and glory, out of love for Him and yearning for His will, blessed be He; and if He does good to it, it will give thanks, and if He afflicts it, it will bear it, and it will surrender its body, soul, and wealth for the sanctification of His name, blessed be He, and will add nothing to this but love of Him and trust in Him - as they said of one of the pious, who would rise at night and say: my God, You have made me hungry and left me naked, and settled me in the darkness of night, and yet You have shown me Your might and Your greatness - even if You burn me with fire, I will add nothing but love of You and rejoicing in You - similar to what Job said (Job 13:15), "though He slay me, yet will I hope in Him." And to this matter the sage alluded when he said (Song of Songs 1:13), "a bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me, lodging between my breasts" - and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Shabbat 88b), by way of exposition, "even though he embitters and angers me, he lodges between my breasts" - and similar to what they said (Berachot 9:5), "and you shall love the LORD your God," and so on, "even if He takes your soul."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:15: And the strongest of the matters through which you may be helped toward this supernal level is the great awe of God and dread of Him, and fear of His commandments, and constant thought of His watchfulness over your hidden and revealed matters, your secrets and your visible deeds, His governance of you and His compassion for you, His knowledge of the hidden and the revealed, of the past and the future of your deeds and thoughts, His doing good to you and drawing you near - and you will not be able, despite all this, to refrain from inclining toward Him in your heart and in your inner being, with a pure heart and complete faith; and your soul will hang in love, and trust in His compassion and the greatness of His grace and mercy, and you will not partner, at that time, with love of Him, love of anything else, and He will not observe you [thinking] that you fear anything besides Him; and you will not be without Him from your thoughts, nor will He depart from before your eyes, and your company will be in solitude, and He will sit with you in the wilderness, and a place full of people will seem in your eyes as though it were empty, and its emptiness of them as though not empty - you will not be desolate when they are present, nor grieve at their absence, and you will always be joyful in God, delighting in your Creator, exulting in His will, yearning to encounter Him - as it is written (Psalms 64:11), "the righteous shall rejoice in the LORD," and the prophet said (Habakkuk 3:18), "yet I will rejoice in the LORD," and David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 27:1), "the LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?" and the rest of that psalm.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:16: And close to these words, it is written in Sefer HaRokeach (Laws of Piety, root of the love of the [divine] Name), in these words: the root of love is that the soul is filled with love of the LORD and bound in the cords of love with joy and gladness of heart, and not like one who serves his master against his will - rather, even if they protested against him, the love burns within him to serve, and he is glad to fulfill the will of his Creator - as the psalmist said (Psalms 100:2), "serve the LORD with gladness," and one serves with uprightness of heart, and "for the upright of heart, gladness" (ibid. 97:11). And he does not serve for his own benefit or his own honor, and he says: what am I, despised and short-lived, here today and in the grave tomorrow? Indeed, I was formed in iniquity and am full of filth - how have I been chosen to be a servant of the King of glory? For when the soul thinks deeply in fear, the flame of love of the heart burns within it, and the joy and gladness of the innermost being increases, and the gladness of the heart and the exultation of the kidneys grows great; a man's wisdom lights up his face, and those who love His name rejoice in Him - for every man in whose heart is the wisdom of the [divine] Name thinks joyfully of the desire to do his Creator's will, to perform His commandments with a whole heart. And the lover does not think of the pleasure of this world, and is not concerned with his wife's excursions, nor with his sons and daughters, and all is as nothing before him - only to perform his Creator's will, and to bring merit to others, and to sanctify His name, and to give himself over in His love - like Abraham (Genesis 14:23), "I have raised my hand to the LORD... that I will not take so much as a thread or a shoelace"; and like Pinchas, who gave himself over when he killed Zimri. And they do not exalt themselves, and do not speak idle words, and do not look at women's faces, and hear their own disgrace and do not respond, and all their thoughts are with their Creator, and they make pleasant songs for their Master, and all the design of their thoughts burns with the fire of His love - happy is he in this world and the next - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:17: And in the book Ta'amei HaMitzvot by Rabbi Yitzchak Ibn Farchi, he wrote concerning the reason for love: that when love is within us, we cause the supernal cherubim to be unified face to face, and there is love between them, and the good oil is poured out upon Malchut, and from there to Metatron and the holy Chayot, and the rest of the worlds are all filled with flow and blessing - to this point, summarizing his intent.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:18: And in the Zohar, Parashat Va'etchanan (263b), they explain concerning the matter of love, in these words: the commandment "to love" - and behold, we have established that the love of the Holy One, blessed be He, requires that a person love Him with abundant love, like Abraham, who feared the Holy One, blessed be He, with such great love that he gave his body and soul over to Him. From here we learn: whoever loves the Holy One, blessed be He, fulfills the Ten Utterances, above and below; and therefore all those ten trials with which Abraham was tested, and in all of which he stood firm, correspond to the Ten Utterances - every trial is an "utterance," and he was tested with that utterance and stood firm in it - and therefore there were ten trials, and Abraham stood firm in all of them, because he was bound and cleaved to the right side of the Holy One, blessed be He, which is Ahavah Rabbah [Great Love].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:19: Why is it called "Great Love"? Because this love stands bound in the supernal world - "everlasting love" - this is the secret of the lower world, without separation, bound to His love, and it is all one secret. And behold, it has already been said, the secret of love: this love rises above all the services of the world; through it the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, is made more precious than everything and is blessed - blessed be He forever and ever - and the secret of love has been stated - to this point. Behold, this discourse explains that the essence of love is to give one's body and soul over for the sanctification of the [divine] Name.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:20: And so they explain in the Tikkunim (page 10b), in these words: "and the wise shall shine" - these are the ones who know the second secret in the commandments, in the word "bereishit" [in the beginning], which is [an anagram of] "ahavah" [love], amounting in a small reckoning to one and the same weight [gematria] - and this is the love of chesed [kindness], which is 72 in numerical value, corresponding to the Name [derived] from the verse "vayisa, vayavo, vayet" [Exodus 14:19-21], which has a vav corresponding to that same number - meaning, the utterance "echad" [one], which is "bereishit" - concerning which it was established of it (Avot 5:1), "could the world not have been created with a single utterance?" And this is the love of one's Master: one who gives his soul over, as one, in love of his Master. And therefore, "and you shall love the LORD your God" - even if He takes your soul; for if his soul is more precious to him than his body, therefore it says "and with all your soul"; and if his body is more precious to him than his money, therefore it says "with all your heart"; and if his money is more precious to him than his body, therefore it says "with all your might [me'od]" - with whatever is precious to you, give it over in love of your Master at a time of distress. And this is the trial with which Israel is destined to be tested in the seventy years of the final exile, when a poor man is considered as one dead, and it is as though his soul were taken - body, soul, and money, all are equal; with whatever is precious to him, he gives it over in love of his Master, and at that time he is bound to the word "ahavah" [love], which is "bereishit," as though the world were created through it. And whoever does not give over his soul, his body, or his money in love of his Master at a time of distress, it is as though he returned the world to chaos and void - and therefore the verse [about chaos and void] is adjacent to it: "and the earth was chaos and void." And whoever gives over his body, his soul, and his money in love of his Master - certainly, in that world, there is none above him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:21: "And you shall love," and so on - this is Malchut, which includes all the sefirot, and it is the commandment of the Holy One, blessed be He, within all 613 commandments; and of it, it is said (Esther 3:3), "why do you transgress the king's commandment?" And it is the building of the world; the evil maidservant is the destruction of the world, and therefore it is said of her, "and the earth was chaos and void" - and it is the strap in the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, to flog the wicked with. And therefore, whoever loves the Holy One, blessed be He, with his soul, or his body, or his money, the Holy One, blessed be He, will guard for him - behold, his love is dependent on what is given to him, and this is not the essence of his love; this is love that, if his money or his body were taken, he would deny Him - this is not the essence of love, until he gives his soul over in love of his Master; and if all three are equally weighted with him, he gives them all over for the sanctification of His name, in love - and this is the essence of love, which is the love of Malchut, which is the love of Chesed, whereas fear is from the side of Gevurah. And from Chesed, Malchut is the love of the yud, as stated; from Gevurah is the fear of the LORD. And the Torah, which is 611 [commandments plus the two heard directly from God], is given from both of them to Israel, and this is the central pillar, called Malchut from its own side: "the Torah of the LORD is perfect" - and it is His commandment, within all 613 commandments that hang from His name - which are "Sh-M-Y" [His Name] with Y-H equals 365 [the negative commandments]; "Z-CH-R-Y" [His remembrance] with V-H equals 248 [the positive commandments] - she is "in His image, according to His likeness."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:22: And in order to understand the words of these discourses, which say that love is to give over one's soul and body for the sanctification of the LORD, we must copy the words of Rashbi concerning the matter of love (Bereshit 11b), where the root of love is explained; in these words: the second commandment - this is the commandment in which the commandment of fear is united and never departs from it, and it is love: for a person to love his Master with a complete love. And what is a "complete love"? This is Ahavah Rabbah [Great Love], as it is written (Genesis 17:1), "walk before Me and be perfect [tamim]" - complete in love. And this is what is written (ibid. 1:3), "and God said, let there be light" - this is the complete love called Ahavah Rabbah, and here is the commandment for a person to love his Master as is fitting.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:23: Rabbi Elazar said: Father, beloved one, I have heard of this love in its completeness. He said to him: say it, my son, before Rabbi Pinchas, for he stands at this level. Rabbi Elazar said: Ahavah Rabbah is a complete love, in the completeness of two sides; and if it is not included in two sides, it is not love as is fitting, in completeness. And therefore we have learned, in two sides is the love of the Holy One, blessed be He, distinguished: there is one who loves Him because he has wealth, length of days, children around him, dominance over his enemies, his ways being set right for him - and because of this he loves Him; but if this were reversed, and the Holy One, blessed be He, brought upon him a cycle of harsh judgment, he would hate Him and not love Him at all - and therefore this love is not a [true, essential] love, for it has [an external] cause. The love called "complete" is one that is present on both sides, whether in judgment or in good, and the fixing of one's ways to love his Master - as we have learned, "even if He takes your soul from you" - this is complete love, present on both sides. And therefore the light of the works of creation went forth and was afterward hidden - when it was hidden, harsh judgment went forth, and the two sides were included together, so that this love be complete as is fitting - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:24: Behold, it is explained from this discourse that the essence of love is to include Chesed within the judgment of Gevurah - and this is "with all your soul": to give over one's soul for the sanctification of the [divine] Name, that when the Holy One, blessed be He, tests him and pours upon him some aspect of judgment, whether small or great, reaching even to the giving over of his soul, out of his abundant love for the Holy One, blessed be He, he will give over his soul and body - such as Chananya, Mishael, and Azarya into the fiery furnace, and many like them. Behold, in this Chesed is included within Gevurah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:25: And so too one must include Gevurah within Chesed - for a person loves the Holy One, blessed be He, from the side of His kindnesses and the abundance of good He bestows upon him, and this is drawn from the side of Chesed; then he should not rely on his good deeds, but rather fear judgment, and say, perhaps sin will cause [a downfall] - along the lines of Jacob, who said (Genesis 32:8), "and Jacob was greatly afraid," as we explained in the Gate of Fear, chapters 3 and 5. It follows that in this Gevurah is included within Chesed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:26: And this is complete love: that there is no completeness for Chesed except with the inclusion of Gevurah within it, and no completeness for Gevurah except with the inclusion of Chesed within it. And the secret is "the LORD, He is God; the LORD, He is God" (I Kings 18:39), as explained (Zohar, Acharei 65a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:27: And for this reason, the word "ahavah" [love] found first in the Torah is concerning Isaac, in the matter of the Binding (Genesis 22:2), "take now your son, your only one, whom you love, Isaac" - meaning, to include Gevurah within Chesed, for "Abraham My beloved" (Isaiah 41:8) refers to Chesed - for love, without qualification, is from the side of Chesed - "Isaac" refers to the Gevurah included within it. And so too, afterward, it is mentioned (ibid. 24:67), "and she became his wife, and he loved her" - from the side of Chesed that was included within it, for through the Binding, which subdued the judgment within him and bound it beneath the Chesed that is Abraham, Chesed was included in him; and therefore there is love in him, which is Chesed, to love Rebecca and bind her to him - as we shall elaborate further on the secret of the love within the Shechinah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:28: It follows that the essence of love is, from the side of judgment, to give over one's soul for the sanctification of the [divine] Name; and since he does not concern himself with his body, created according to nature under the name Elohim, he is then sanctified in the love of Chesed, and Chesed overcomes judgment - for all the workings of the world are conducted according to nature [teva], which is Elohim.
